definitions.explanation: In medieval Japan, a blind performer in monk's dress who recited stories, above all the Tale of the Heike, to the accompaniment of the biwa, a lute.

examples.japanese: {琵琶法師|びわほうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{語|かた}る→語る：01930_kataru⟧。
examples.english: A biwa minstrel recites a tale.

examples.japanese: ⟦{平家物語|へいけものがたり}→平家物語：31060_heikemonogatari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{琵琶法師|びわほうし}⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧⟦{語|かた}り{継|つ}がれた→語り継ぐ：22312_kataritsugu⟧。
examples.english: The Tale of the Heike was handed down by biwa minstrels.

examples.japanese: ⟦{怪談|かいだん}→怪談：12608_kaidan⟧「{耳|みみ}なし{芳一|ほういち}」⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{平家|へいけ}→平家：31857_heike⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{亡霊|ぼうれい}→亡霊：11473_bourei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれた→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦{盲目|もうもく}→盲目：13727_moumoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{琵琶法師|びわほうし}だ。
examples.english: The hero of the ghost story "Earless Hoichi" is a blind biwa minstrel summoned by the ghosts of the Heike.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The {琵琶法師|びわほうし} are the reason the ⟦{平家物語|へいけものがたり}→平家物語：31060_heikemonogatari⟧ survives as a spoken, chanted text as well as a written one; their recitation is called {平曲|へいきょく}. School textbooks introduce them alongside the opening lines ⟦{祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}→祇園精舎：31902_gionshouja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧. Lafcadio Hearn's retelling of {耳|みみ}なし{芳一|ほういち} made one of them famous abroad.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{盲目|もうもく}→盲目：13727_moumoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{琵琶法師|びわほうし}: a blind biwa minstrel
- {琵琶法師|びわほうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{語|かた}る→語る：01930_kataru⟧: a biwa minstrel recites
